rationale: Edge-case lens finding verified against source: withinWindow()'s strict `<` comparison drops a native session's own final usage record whenever its ts equals observedEnd, which is the common case since observedEnd is computed as the max of the session's own message timestamps (native-loader.ts) — a correctness regression introduced by this diff's own fix, kept as CR-002/major. Standards audit (coverage_gap: false) flagged one blocking code-quality violation (CR-001/major): new grouping logic added inline into the already-oversized enrichCosts()/cost-enricher.ts instead of being extracted. Acceptance lens did not run (genuine no-spec — no story/spec artifact existed), which forces confidence to low per the no-spec rule; blind and verification-gap are n/a for the balanced profile, not a coverage gap. 1 finding deferred (startTime defaults to 0 for a fully unbounded session, pre-existing earliest-wins dedupe design the new windowEnd filter was never meant to cover) and 3 dismissed as noise after verifying against source: a theoretical bad-endTime guard with no reachable producer, an observedStart/observedEnd asymmetry whose fallback computation already yields equivalent timeline bounds, and a cosmetic file-path-identity concern on a display-only value explicitly commented as such in the source.

findings.title: New grouping block inlined into oversized function
findings.problem: enrichCosts() was already ~160 lines inside a 546-line file; the diff adds a new ~20-line reportedObservedEnd/byFilePath grouping block (lines ~419-434) directly into that function instead of extracting a helper, growing the file to 568 lines.
findings.impact: Violates the project's documented 'functions under 50 lines / one responsibility' and 'files under 500 lines' standards, compounding an existing violation instead of containing it, which blocks the code-quality gate.
findings.recommendation: Extract the byFilePath grouping and reportedObservedEnd computation into a small named helper (e.g. computeReportedObservedEnd(ordered: ParsedEntry[]): Map<string, number>) with its own JSDoc, called from enrichCosts.

findings.title: Window filter drops session's own final turn
findings.problem: withinWindow() filters records with `r.ts === null || r.ts < windowEnd` (strict less-than). windowEnd is entry.observedEnd, which for native/untracked sessions (native-loader.ts's claudeFamilyBounds / synthesizeCodexRawSession) is computed as the max timestamp across the session's own messages — the same field extractClaudeUsageRecords reads as a usage record's own `ts`. So the final usage-bearing message's ts commonly equals windowEnd exactly and fails the strict comparison.
findings.impact: The final turn's token usage is silently excluded from that session's own cost total for most native sessions, not only the shared-log scenario the fix targets — a new, systematic undercount introduced by the very change meant to correct cost attribution for EPMCDME-15316 Root Cause A. The added cost-enricher.test.ts case for this commit uses a synthetic endEvent decoupled from message content, so it never exercises the ts === windowEnd boundary and would not catch this.
findings.recommendation: Change the filter to an inclusive bound (`r.ts === null || r.ts <= windowEnd`), or otherwise make the boundary convention consistent with how observedEnd is derived; add a cost-enricher.test.ts case where a session's own last usage record's ts equals its own observedEnd.
